interpretation: All twelve balanced 1x attempts pass. All 576 replacements and 576 insert dispatches preserve exact expected text, links and underline. Twelve native browser insert controls pass. All file fixtures remain unchanged.

Observed editor plugins fall from 104 to 98. Link plugins fall from six to three. Each mark occurs once, and all candidate duplicate-extension warnings disappear. These are deterministic work/configuration counts, not a latency reduction.

Dense-plan synchronous insertion has a 1.10% median paired reduction with three faster and three slower pairs. Dense replacement has a 2.36% median paired increase, with four slower pairs. Short-plan synchronous medians are also mixed and worse in their median paired results. No reliable performance gain follows.
All sixteen metric rows, all operation observations, all startup-readiness bounds and all attempts are preserved. No passed-only subset or pooled confirmation is used.
Keep the independent link-click and duplicate-registration correctness fix. Give it no credit toward the 20% normal-streaming target.
limits: These are synchronous real-editor commands and dispatches on a dense task view. They do not measure full-view streaming or editor construction time.
Two-animation-frame readiness is an upper bound. It is not field INP or screen presentation.
The browser is Linux HeadlessChrome with ANGLE SwiftShader software rendering. No M2 Air, battery or memory-leak conclusion follows.
The 400-step document has 75988 input bytes. It is a dense controlled plan, not a claim about the size of the user plan.
The final original-baseline matrix and 20% normal-streaming target remain open.
nextAction: Inspect the preserved normal production rendering trace for forced layout and invalidation attribution before selecting another optimization. Keep existing motion visibility and native interaction policies intact.
